title: device-map fragmentation + KV-shadow metadata leak causing intermittent tenant OOMs in private clusters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers running Private and Dedicated clusters reported intermittent GPU OOM cascades over the last three weeks. Investigation shows two correlated failure modes: (1) device-map fragmentation — small unreachable allocations accumulating on the device allocator across long-lived sessions, and (2) a KV-shadow metadata leak that pins small metadata objects in host memory which prevents efficient defragmentation. Together these cause a slow memory spiral that eventually triggers OOM on high-concurrency workloads. This ticket tracks investigation, hotpatch PR, rollout, and postmortem for affected customers (Customer A, Customer B internal escalations).
observed_behavior: Gradual memory growth on GPU and host over 12-48 hours without matching increase in token throughput
OOM stack shows runtime tensor arena allocation failure followed by KV cache eviction thrash
Affected clusters: private-vpc-us-west-2 (Customer A), dedicated-gpupool-eu (Customer B), and one hosted nodegroup in us-east-1 encountered transient OOMs during burst testing
reproduction_steps: Run long-lived streaming chat workload (avg session length > 120s) with KV cache enabled and high concurrent sessions (200+)
Observe allocator free list growth: ephemeral allocations returned but not coalesced in device-map (see allocator trace logs)
Trigger synthetic stress: repeated session handoff + token prefix cache churn to accelerate leak path
root_cause: A race in the device-map free/coalesce path combined with an incomplete tombstone cleanup in the KV-shadow metadata reconciler. On session teardown the metadata tombstone flag was set but not enqueued for background compaction when certain eviction paths executed concurrently. The device allocator therefore accumulated many tiny free entries that were not merged, increasing fragmentation and preventing large contiguous allocations which led to GPU OOMs under burst conditions.
mitigation_short_term: Applied a node-local livepatch that forces periodic device-map coalescing and enqueues KV-shadow tombstones for compaction every 60s. This reduced OOM frequency for affected customers by ~85% during the canary window.
resolution_summary: Hotpatch merged to runtime branch and promoted to canary pool. PR includes a conservative mutex around coalesce path and a gated background tombstone enqueuer for KV-shadow. We rejected more invasive lock-free rewrite for this release due to time and regression risk; iterative follow-ups planned.
canary_results: Canary window: 72 hours on 10% of dedicated pool + two private clusters
Observed total OOMs dropped from median 3/day to 0-1/day during window
Latency P95 unchanged; token throughput increased slightly due to reduced eviction churn
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy hotpatch to 10% of Dedicated and two affected Private clusters (complete)
Phase 2 (staged): expand to 50% Dedicated and additional Private customer clusters over 48 hours with telemetry gates
Phase 3 (global): full rollout if no regression after 72 hours, include hosted rolling restart window low-traffic period
Rollback: artifactized previous runtime binary + automated rollback playbook in ops-runbook
test_plan: Add unit tests covering tombstone enqueue paths
Add integration test that simulates concurrent eviction + session teardown to assert device-map coalescing correctness
Add e2e soak test (48h) with replayed customer trace (Customer A) in CI cluster
monitoring_and_alerts: New dashboard tile: tenant memory slope + kv-shadow tombstone backlog
Pager rule: P0 page to oncall if tenant OOMs spike by >50% vs baseline after rollout
review_feedback: Security review: micro-lock introduces low contention but acceptable for short term (Security approved 2026-02-25)
SRE: requested conservative backoff logic in enqueuer (implemented in PR-2918)
PM: require customer-facing summary and support playbook before Phase 2 expansion
open_followups: Investigate lock-free coalesce redesign (RFC due Q2)
Add KV-shadow metadata size quotas and stronger observability for host-side metadata growth
Run broader fragmentation fuzzing harness against allocator in CI (owner: Memory tooling)
Create KB entry for Support with troubleshooting steps and temporary mitigations
support_notes: Temporary mitigation for customers: enable aggressive per-session eviction and restart agent every 24h as interim (ops runbook)
Support message drafted and approved by PM (Customer A and B contacted 2026-02-28)
Root-cause summary provided to customers and next-steps scheduled for March 15 technical review
final_status_decision: Pending completion of Phase 3 and two-week monitoring window. If stable, close as Done and track lock-free refactor as a separate EPIC.
notes: This ticket intentionally keeps change conservative to avoid regressing high-throughput code paths
We prioritized rapid customer relief over ideal long-term design. Follow-ups are required to remove mutex in favor of scalable approach
Cross-team sync scheduled with SRE, Platform, and Support on 2026-03-16 to finalize rollout cadence
